Where it began

Ishan Kishan was born in Patna, Bihar, on 18 July 1998, and went to Delhi Public School in the city. His family's roots lie in a village in Aurangabad district. When he was starting out, Bihar's cricket association and the national board could not settle their differences, so he crossed the state line and made his name with neighbouring Jharkhand.

The move worked out well for both. He captained India at the Under-19 World Cup in 2016, and that same year made 273 against Delhi in the Ranji Trophy, a record for a Jharkhand batter.

The player

Kishan is a wicketkeeper who, bat in hand, likes to get on with it. His two Tests came in 2023: he made 78 runs for once out, including an unbeaten 52, and took five catches behind the stumps. By November 2026 those two matches were his whole Test career, which leaves him with an average of 78.00 and nothing to apologise for.

The shorter formats have seen more of him. On his international debut, a Twenty20 against England in 2021, he made 56 off 32 balls and was player of the match. In a one-day international against Bangladesh in December 2022 he made 210 off 131 balls, reaching 200 faster than anyone before him. In 2026 he made his first Twenty20 hundred for India against New Zealand and played his part in a T20 World Cup win.

What made him special

He hits the ball cleanly and hard, often from the first ball he faces. In the 2020 IPL he struck more sixes than anyone, and in the 2025–26 season he captained Jharkhand to their first Syed Mushtaq Ali title, making a hundred in the final himself. He has also turned out to be a natural leader, captaining Jharkhand, East Zone and, for a while in 2026, Sunrisers Hyderabad.

Patience has not always been his favourite virtue. Then again, when a batter can score 76 in 32 balls, waiting around would seem a waste.

Away from the middle

He made his IPL name with Mumbai Indians, finishing as their leading run-scorer in 2020, and in 2025 scored a hundred on his first appearance for Sunrisers Hyderabad. That summer he also had a short spell with Nottinghamshire and made 87 on his debut at Trent Bridge.

And finally

On that Nottinghamshire debut he held a catch off the very first ball he kept to. For a man who likes to start quickly, it was perfectly in character.
